DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph OPINION NO. s. 20. SEP 26 HON. ZIFFRED A. ANCHETA President Liga ng mga Barangay-NCR Dear Hon. Ancheta: This refers to your letter dated May 26, 2023 requesting legal opinion on whether the local chief executive of cities and municipalities have the power to review and approve the barangay budget appropriation ordinance. Cited in your letter are Sections 54 (c) and 333 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code), which read, respectively, thus: "Section 54. Approval of Ordinances. — (a) Xxx (b) Xxx (c) Ordinances enacted by the sangguniang barangay shall, upon approval by the majority of all its members, be signed by the punong barangay. "Section 333. Review of the Barangay Budget. - (a) Within ten (IO) days from its approval, copies of the barangay ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations shall be furnished the sangguniang panlungsod or the sangguniang bayan, as the case may be, through the city or municipal budget officer. The sanggunian concerned shall have the power to review such ordinance in order to ensure that the provisions of this Title are complied with. If within sixty (60) days after the receipt of the ordinance, the sanggunian concerned takes no action thereon, the same shall continue to be in full force and effect. If within the same period, the sanggunian concerned shall have ascertained that the ordinance contains appropriations in excess of the estimates of the income duly certified as collectible, or that the same has not complied with the budgetary requirements set forth in this Title, the said ordinance shall be declared inoperative in its entirety or in part. Items of appropriation contrary to, or in excess of, any of the general limitations or the maximum amount prescribed in this Title shall be disallowed or reduced accordingly." "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The foregoing provisions, as well as Section 444 and 455 of the Code, provide no clear indication of the power of the city/municipal mayor to review and approve the barangay budget appropriation ordinance. Hence, your request for legal opinion. At the outset, there are two important matters that warrant discussion: (I) approval; and (2) review of the barangay budget appropriation ordinance. Insofar as the approval of ordinances enacted by the sangguniang barangay is concerned, Section 54 of the Code, as above-cited, is instructive. As could be clearly gleaned, ordinances enacted by the sangguniang barangay need not be approved by the city or municipal mayor where the barangay belongs. The Code is clear in that the approval of ordinances enacted by the sangguniang barangay is contingent upon the approval of the majority of all its members—by 'its' meaning the sangguniang barangay members concerned—after which the punong barangay shall sign such ordinance. Accordingly, the approval of sangguniang barangay ordinances is solely a barangay matter—the Code does not require the involvement of the city/ municipal mayor or the sangguniang panlungsod or bayan for that matter. After approval, the ordinance authorizing the barangay annual budget shall be transmitted to the sangguniang panlungsod/bayan, through the city or municipal budget officer, for review pursuant to the mandate of Section 333 of the LGC. At this juncture, may we stress that pending review by the sangguniang panlungsod/bayan, such barangay ordinance authorizing the annual budget can be validly enforced (e.g. funds can already be disbursed) because effectivity is determined not upon review thereof but rather in accordance with Section 332 of the LGC. Hence, the ordinance enacting the annual budget shall take effect at the beginning of the ensuing calendar year. Said ordinance authorizing the annual budget shall continue to be in full force and effect unless and until within sixty (60) days from receipt of the said ordinance, the sangguniang panglungsod/byan shall have ascertained that the ordinance contains appropriations in excess of the estimates of the income duly certified as collectible, or that the same has not complied with the budgetary requirements set forth in Title V, in which case, the said ordinance would be inoperative upon declaration by the sanggunian to that effect. With the advice of such action taken by the sanggunian, the latter shall return the barangay ordinance, through the city or municipal budget officer, to the punong barangay for proper adjustmentsl. As could be clearly gathered from the aforequoted provisions, it is the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguning bayan—as the case may be—who has the power to review the barangay budget and not the city or municipal mayor. This is precisely because the review of such ordinances is fundamentally a legislative function specifically lodged with the legislative body—the sanggunian. 1 DILG Opinion No. 12, S. 2008 dated March 12, 2008 Page 2 of 3

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you.
